name: Sicilian Scheveningen — Main Lines
description: One of the most dynamic Sicilian systems. Black builds a solid pawn chain on d6-e6, keeping maximum flexibility. White can attack with the English Attack (f3+g4), Keres Attack (g4), or Classical Be2. The Scheveningen is a battleground of the highest order.

lines.name: Classical Variation — Be2
lines.description: White develops naturally with 6.Be2, aiming for a solid kingside attack after castling. The most positionally sound approach — White builds with f4 and a central bind.

lines.name: English Attack — f3 & g4
lines.description: White launches the English Attack with 6.Be3, 7.f3, and 8.Qd2 after 7...b5. Black develops 8...Nbd7, White storms with 9.g4 h6, and castles long 10.O-O-O as Black plays 10...Bb7. The thematic clash follows: 11.h4 b4 12.Na4 — and Black strikes back in the center with 12...d5!, the critical counter in the English Attack.

lines.name: Keres Attack — g4
lines.description: White plays the immediate 6.g4 — the Keres Attack. After 6...h6 7.h4 Nc6 8.g5 hxg5, White recaptures 9.Bxg5!, keeping the kingside tension. Black develops 9...Be7, White prepares long castling with 10.Qd2, and Black fires the thematic central break 10...d5!.

lines.name: Scheveningen — f4 System
lines.description: White grabs space with the early 6.f4 against the Scheveningen, aiming for a central squeeze. Black develops solidly with ...Nc6 and ...Be7, castles, and meets White's setup with the queenside ...a6/...b6 plan and a rook to c8. A strategic battle of space versus flexibility.
